paragraphs: Two layers, from examples/26, both on context. Every backend call runs under context.WithTimeout, so http.Client gives up after 2 seconds; the request context is the parent, so a client that disconnects also cancels the call. The deadline endpoint derives a context from the caller's remaining budget and sends the same number in the X-Deadline-Ms header, so the backend can refuse work it cannot finish.

paragraphs: cenkalti/backoff v7: backoff.Retry calls the function until it succeeds, the tries run out, the elapsed-time cap passes or the request context ends. The exponential policy starts at 100 ms, doubles up to 2 seconds and randomises each wait by up to half. When it gives up, AsRetryError exposes the last real error rather than the stop reason. Retry only idempotent calls, and pair the retry with a circuit breaker.

paragraphs: sony/gobreaker v2 with generics: ReadyToTrip opens the breaker after five consecutive failures, Timeout keeps it open for ten seconds, and MaxRequests lets two trial calls through in half-open, both of which must succeed to close it. Execute returns ErrOpenState or ErrTooManyRequests without calling the backend, and the handler answers from its fallback with the reason; errors.AsType picks out the upstream status. One breaker per dependency.
